Match the treated patients once per propensity model

Source: R/match_each_model.R
match_each_model.Rd

Runs 1:1 nearest-neighbour matching for the average treatment effect in the treated (ATT) once per model of a fit_propensity_models() object, each time calling MatchIt::matchit() with that model's logit column as a numeric distance Every matching option is passed explicitly, so a future change of a MatchIt default cannot alter the results. All models are matched, whether or not they passed the log-loss gate; the gate is applied later by the wrapper propensity_sensitivity().

Usage

match_each_model(
  model_set,
  data,
  replace = TRUE,
  ratio = 1,
  m_order = "largest",
  caliper = NULL,
  oracle_logit = NULL,
  bootstrap_samples = 0,
  cores = 1,
  seed = 1,
  common_random_order = FALSE,
  clip_bootstrap = FALSE
)

# S3 method for class 'match_set'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

model_set

A propensity_model_set from fit_propensity_models().

data

The data frame the model set was fitted on (same rows, same order). The matches are stored with the row names of data as ids; the data itself is not stored.

replace

TRUE (matching with replacement; the default of this function) or FALSE (without replacement; the default of propensity_sensitivity() with a formula). Both are supported; see vignette("definitions", package = "propsens") for what each targets.

ratio

Number of untreated partners per treated patient. Only 1 is supported in this version.

m_order

Order in which treated patients are matched; one of MatchIt's "largest", "smallest", "data", "random", "closest", "farthest".

caliper

NULL (default, no caliper) or a positive number: the caliper in standard deviations of the logit.

oracle_logit

Internal, for simulation studies only: a numeric vector of length n with the true logit, for example the true_logit column of simulate_example_data(). When given, one extra entry oracle is matched with the same options. Not needed in an analysis.

bootstrap_samples

Number of bootstrap samples B for the sampling-instability block (default 0, none).

cores

Number of cores for the matching tasks (default 1).

seed

Integer seed from which every other seed is derived.

common_random_order

Internal, for simulation studies only, and only for m_order = "random": FALSE (default) gives each model its own random order; TRUE gives every model (and the oracle) the same random order, so that the models differ only in their distances, not in the order in which treated patients are matched.

clip_bootstrap

FALSE (default) or TRUE: clip the bootstrap refits' scores to [clip, 1 - clip] with the model set's clip, as the cross-fitted scores are. See the section "Bootstrap block".

x

A match_set object.

...

Not used.

Value

An object of class "match_set": a list with

  • matches: one data frame per model (treated_id, control_id, weight, pair_id), named by model id;

  • weights: n x M matrix of MatchIt weights, rows named by the row ids;

  • treated_kept: named vector, share of treated patients that were matched;

  • calls: named character vector with the deparsed matchit() call of each model; the call names the data and the model set as the caller wrote them and re-evaluates to the same matches;

  • oracle: NULL, or a list with matches, weights, treated_kept and call;

  • bootstrap: NULL, or a list with rank, pairs, present (n x B matrices) and skipped (data frame of skipped samples with the reason) and design_rule_samples (the samples whose refit used the design-matrix rule for a level absent from the sample) and prediction_fallback_samples (the samples whose refit used it because prediction failed);

  • models: the model table of the model set (model_id, algorithm, seed_index, passed_logloss_gate), used by the diagnostics to apply the quality gate;

  • model_ids, treatment, row_ids, settings and call.

Matching options

The call is MatchIt::matchit(formula, data, method = "nearest", estimand = "ATT", distance = <logit column>, replace = replace, ratio = 1, m.order = m_order, caliper = caliper, std.caliper = TRUE, normalize = FALSE). The order "largest" is MatchIt's default for the ATT when a numeric distance is supplied: the treated patient with the largest score is matched first. A caliper is given in standard deviations of the logit (std.caliper = TRUE); it drops treated patients, so the share of treated kept is reported.

Weights

normalize = FALSE is passed so that MatchIt's weights are the raw matching weights: every matched treated patient has weight 1, every matched untreated patient has weight equal to the number of pairs it belongs to, and unmatched patients have weight 0. The sum of the weights of the untreated patients is therefore the number of matched treated patients, also with replacement. (MatchIt's default normalize = TRUE rescales those weights to a mean of 1, which changes no weighted mean or balance statistic but would make that sum equal the number of distinct untreated partners.) Each row of a match table carries weight = 1 / ratio, which is 1 in this version.

Bootstrap block

With bootstrap_samples = B > 0 the function draws B nonparametric row bootstrap samples of the data (one derived seed per sample). A sample with fewer than 10 treated or 10 untreated rows is skipped, listed in bootstrap$skipped and counted in a message. For each sample, logistic regression with the model set's formula (as written, with any interactions or transformations) is fitted in-sample, without cross-fitting: this block measures the sampling variability of the fitted model, not its out-of-sample accuracy (see bootstrap_rank_instability()). The refitted model predicts logits for every ORIGINAL patient; their percentile ranks form bootstrap$rank (n x B). These logits are not clipped by default, while the cross-fitted scores are clipped to [clip, 1 - clip]; under near-separation many cross-fitted scores can then share the clipped value (tied ranks) while their bootstrap ranks stay distinct. clip_bootstrap = TRUE clips the bootstrap scores in the same way. The default (FALSE) keeps the method as it was studied. When a factor level of the original data is absent from the sample, the refit uses the full-data design matrix and scores those patients as the reference level (the rule of the cross-fitted logistic model); the samples concerned are listed in bootstrap$design_rule_samples. When every level is present but prediction from the refitted model fails (a rank-deficient fit that did not converge), the refit uses the same design-matrix rule; those samples are listed in bootstrap$prediction_fallback_samples. No sample is skipped for this reason. The sample is then matched with the same options, rows are mapped back to original ids, and for every original treated patient present in the sample the untreated partner matched to its first occurrence is stored in bootstrap$pairs (n x B, NA when absent or unmatched). bootstrap$present (n x B, logical) says whether each original patient is in each sample. A skipped sample keeps its column, filled with NA, so that every matrix is n x B.

Seeds and parallel runs

Per-task seeds are derived in the main process from seed, passed to each worker and applied with withr::with_seed(); m_order = "random" and the bootstrap draws are therefore reproducible and identical for cores = 1 and cores > 1. The matching tasks, the bootstrap draws and the bootstrap matching each have their own family of derived seeds, separate from the model fits; with the default order "largest" matching uses no random numbers. Parallel runs use parallel::mclapply() on Unix; on Windows the run is serial.

Examples

data("lalonde", package = "MatchIt")
model_set <- fit_propensity_models(
  treat ~ age + educ + race + married + nodegree + re74 + re75,
  data = lalonde, seeds = 1, n_trees = 100,
  algorithms = c("logistic_regression", "random_forest", "gradient_boosting")
)
with_replacement <- match_each_model(model_set, lalonde, replace = TRUE)
with_replacement
#> Match set: 3 model(s), 614 patients, 185 treated
#> Matching: 1:1 nearest neighbour on the logit, ATT, with replacement, order "largest", caliper none
#>               model_id treated_kept distinct_controls
#>  logistic_regression_1            1                85
#>        random_forest_1            1                77
#>    gradient_boosting_1            1                69
head(with_replacement$matches$logistic_regression_1)
#>   treated_id control_id weight pair_id
#> 1       NSW1    PSID157      1       1
#> 2       NSW2    PSID224      1       2
#> 3       NSW3    PSID335      1       3
#> 4       NSW4     PSID15      1       4
#> 5       NSW5    PSID401      1       5
#> 6       NSW6    PSID134      1       6
without_replacement <- match_each_model(model_set, lalonde, replace = FALSE,
                                        bootstrap_samples = 5)
without_replacement
#> Match set: 3 model(s), 614 patients, 185 treated
#> Matching: 1:1 nearest neighbour on the logit, ATT, without replacement, order "largest", caliper none
#>               model_id treated_kept distinct_controls
#>  logistic_regression_1            1               185
#>        random_forest_1            1               185
#>    gradient_boosting_1            1               185
#> Bootstrap: 5 logistic refits (0 sample(s) skipped)
dim(without_replacement$bootstrap$rank)
#> [1] 614   5
